attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (Python HTTP API on port 8080 serving /health and /inventory), protected with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 so the kernel OOM killer deprioritizes it. Verified the protection by running a controlled memory-hog process (default oom_score_adj=0) that drove the node to full memory exhaustion; the kernel's global OOM killer killed the hog (pid 1393, oom_score_adj:0) while inventory-api (pid 1295, oom_score_adj:-1000) was never touched and kept serving requests throughout and after. Cleaned up the hog service/files. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and healthy service state pre-reboot, issued systemctl reboot with the ack returned before disconnection, polled until the node came back, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified inventory-api auto-started, is active, retains its OOM protection, and serves correct data post-reboot.
